notes.meaning: People are warned not to boast about what they will do tomorrow, because no one can know what a day will bring. Planning ahead is wise, but acting as if we control the future is foolish presumption. We ought to hold our plans loosely and trust God with each day.

Praise should come from other people, not from our own mouths. Boasting about our own achievements shows pride and self-love, and it often turns people away. Good deeds will speak for themselves when others notice them.

Heavy rocks and piles of sand are burdensome to carry, but the trouble caused by an angry fool is far heavier. A foolish person lacks self-control and explodes without good reason, wearing out anyone nearby. Bearing the weight of someone's unreasonable rage is exhausting and painful.

Sudden fury is cruel, and uncontrolled anger sweeps over people like a flood. Yet jealousy is even harder to survive, because it hides in the heart and refuses to fade away. While anger often cools down after an outburst, jealousy keeps brooding and plotting harm.

An honest correction spoken out loud is better than love that stays hidden and does nothing. True love takes courage and speaks up when a friend is wandering into danger. Keeping quiet when a friend needs help is not kindness at all.

Painful words from a faithful friend can be trusted, because they are spoken to heal and protect us. In contrast, an enemy may shower us with kisses and flattering words while hiding bad intentions. We should welcome hard truths from people who care about us rather than sweet lies from opponents.

A person who is completely full will turn away even sweet honey, but a starving person finds delight in anything bitter. Having too much can make people ungrateful and dissatisfied, while hunger teaches people to value simple things. In the same way, proud people look down on God's truth, but those who feel their spiritual need welcome it gladly.

A person who wanders away from home is like a bird that strays from its nest. Leaving behind one's family, calling, and place of safety brings danger and misery. God gives us places and responsibilities where we are meant to remain settled and faithful.

Sweet-smelling oils and burning incense bring joy to the senses and cheer up the heart. In the same way, the warm, heartfelt advice of a close friend brings comfort and strength to the inner life. Having a trusted companion to guide us through tough choices is a sweet gift.

Longtime family friends should not be abandoned when hard times arrive. In a sudden emergency, a reliable neighbor who is close by can help much faster than a distant relative. Strong friendships built on years of trust are often more dependable than family ties that are far away.

A father urges his son to become wise so that the parent's heart will be glad. A wise child brings honor to his parents and silences anyone who criticizes how they raised him. Living with wisdom brings credit to our family and teachers.

Sensible people see trouble coming and take shelter before it strikes. Foolish and careless people keep walking blindly forward and end up paying a heavy price. Prudence means keeping our eyes open so we can avoid unnecessary danger.

If a person is foolish enough to guarantee a loan for a stranger, the lender should demand his coat as security. Anyone who risks his own money on people he barely knows is heading straight for poverty. Taking collateral protects against the foolish promises of someone who cannot be trusted.

Shouting loud praises to a neighbor early in the morning will be treated like a curse rather than a blessing. Over-the-top flattery delivered at the wrong time sounds insincere and quickly annoys everyone around. Genuine praise is quiet, thoughtful, and shared with proper consideration for others.

A quarrelsome wife is compared to the steady drip of rain leaking through a roof during a storm. Trying to stop her arguments is as impossible as holding back the wind or trying to grab slippery oil with your hand. A home filled with constant bickering robs the family of peace and shelter.

Just as two iron blades rub together to make each other sharp, friends sharpen one another through honest conversation. Good fellowship brightens a person's mind, strengthens their character, and encourages good deeds. We grow wiser when we let godly friends challenge and sharpen us.

A worker who takes good care of a fig tree gets to enjoy its sweet fruit, and a servant who looks after his master receives honor. Faithful, patient work in ordinary duties brings a sure reward over time. God honors those who do their daily tasks with diligence and care.

Just as calm water reflects a person's face, the heart reveals what a person is really like. Our hidden thoughts, desires, and motives show our true character far better than any outward appearance. By looking honestly at our own inner thoughts, we discover who we truly are.

The grave and the place of death are never satisfied with how many bodies they take. Human eyes and desires are just as hungry, always wanting more wealth, pleasure, and power. True contentment cannot come from worldly things, but only from God.

Silver is tested in a melting pot and gold in a furnace, but a person is tested by the praise they receive. Compliments show what is inside: a proud person becomes arrogant, while a wise person stays humble and thankful. How we react to applause reveals the real strength of our character.

Even if you pound a foolish person in a bowl with a pestle like grain, his foolishness will not leave him. Stubborn foolishness can become so deeply set in a person that even severe punishment fails to cure it. When a person hardens his heart against correction, only God's grace—His unearned favor—can heal him.

A shepherd is told to know the health of his sheep and pay close attention to his herds. Earthly riches do not last forever, and even a king's crown is not guaranteed to pass to every generation. Diligent care of what God has placed in our hands is necessary because wealth can easily fade away.

When the hay is cleared away and new green grass appears on the hills, the flock provides for all the shepherd's needs. Lambs supply wool for warm clothes, goats provide money to buy land, and their rich milk feeds the whole household. God meets our daily needs through honest labor and the steady cycles of nature.
